title: Kernel warmstart orbiter with prefill bucketing and online bandit autocalibration
creator: Nina Park
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight "orbiter" layer in the runtime that performs warmstart kernel selection using a combination of architecture fingerprints, per-request meta-features, and small online bandit experiments. This ticket covers the heuristic design, microbenchmark harness, safe fallback policy, rollout strategy, and telemetry needed to ship a production-safe autotuner for mixed prefill/decode workloads.

Background: Current kernel selection uses static heuristics plus an offline catalog of microbenchmarks. We see latency tail regressions on variable-length streams and bursty prefill-heavy traffic. A persistent problem is cold-start for rarely used (model, seq_len) pairs and suboptimal kernel choices when hardware topology or quantization variant changes.

Design summary:
- Prefill bucketing: maintain lightweight histogram buckets keyed by coarse seqlen ranges (e.g., 1-16, 17-64, 65-256, 257-1024) plus request-phase tag (prefill vs decode). Each bucket records rolling aggregates (p50,p95,p99 latency, token throughput, memory high-water). Buckets are sized to keep memory cost < 1% of node.
- Architecture fingerprint: on node startup collect GPU topology, compute capability, SM count, CUDA driver version, memory bandwidth estimate and encode into a short stable fingerprint. Fingerprint maps to kernel compatibility groups.
- Warmstart candidate list: for each (model, bucket, fingerprint) keep a prioritized list of 3 kernel variants (fastest-known, safe-fallback, exploration-candidate). Populate from offline catalog + recent telemetry.
- Online bandit probe: when a request falls into a bucket with low confidence, run lightweight epsilon-greedy probes at a low rate (configurable, default 1% of requests) to try exploration-candidate. Track reward as latency + soft-penalty for OOM/queueing. Decay exploration rate once sufficient confidence achieved.
- Safety and rollback: enforce strict SLO guardrails — any probe causing >2x p95 increase or an OOM must trigger immediate local rollback and sample flagged for investigation. Global circuit breaker in control plane to disable orbiter if regressions exceed threshold across nodes.
- Telemetry: emit per-bucket metrics, probe outcomes, kernel-selection trace for each request (small key-value), and daily heatmap summaries. Include tags for release, node-fingerprint, and model-version.

Trade-offs:
- Pros: faster convergence to good kernels for niche combinations, reduced manual tuning, graceful exploration.
- Cons: extra complexity, small probe-induced noise for a subset of requests, need for robust telemetry and observability.

Success metrics (to be measured in runtime-1.22 canary):
- p95 overall token latency improvement for mixed workload >= 5% vs baseline for at least 50% of model/bucket combos.
- No customer-facing latency SLO violations attributable to probes during rollout.
- Reduction in manual kernel-override tickets by 30% in first 3 months.
acceptance_criteria: Orbiter builds and can be toggled via node runtime flag
Prefill buckets populated and visible in telemetry dashboards
Online probes run at configured rate and collect reward signals
Circuit breaker automatically disables orbiter on detected regressions
Canary rollout demonstrates no net increase in SLO violations for 7 continuous days
Documentation (design doc + runbook) published and linked in ticket
